Done. crates/cs-archive/src/reader.rs implements the ADR 18:393 contract: ArchiveReader::files(source_id) -> Vec<ArchivedFile> and read(&file) -> Vec<u8>, yielding (logical_path, bytes) so no importer learns whether its source was mirrored or bundled. Carries the ADR 7 determinism fix — sorts on the string form of the logical path, because Path's component-wise Ord puts <id>/subagents/x.jsonl before <id>.jsonl and a string compare does the opposite, which silently changes which file wins a metadata merge. Test files_are_returned_in_string_sorted_logical_order pins exactly that. Bundle unpacking is not implemented, but no source uses layout=bundle yet; that work is chat-search-a7k.7.

Done. crates/cs/src/query.rs:29-54 drives indexing entirely through ArchiveReader over the machine dir — reader.files(&source.id) then reader.read(f) — never ~/.codex/sessions or ~/.claude/projects. Both importers are pure functions over bytes (codex::import(logical_path, bytes), claude_code::import(logical_path, bytes)) with no filesystem access, which is what makes retroactive reparse work (ADR 1). One residue: the ChatGPT export at query.rs:63-79 is still read straight from a directory via --chatgpt-export, and that is already tracked as chat-search-6eb.7 (P0) and chat-search-a7k.8. Ordering trap 2 in docs/BACKLOG.md is discharged.

Superseded by chat-search-me9.1's design. A generation counter exists to discard results from a query that is still in flight when a newer keystroke arrives. Our search is synchronous in the event loop at 1.4-6.4 ms, so there is never an in-flight query to go stale and the counter guards nothing. fast-resume needs search_generation and applied_search_generation because Tantivy plus a background rescan is genuinely async; we are not. Reinstate trigger recorded on me9.1: if any keystroke path exceeds ~30 ms — most likely via the query DSL (chat-search-6eb.11) or fuzzy-on-failure (chat-search-6eb.10) — the search stops being synchronous and this comes back.

Done, verified. docs/DECISIONS.md:210 now carries '## 14. Client seam: no daemon — link the core in Rust, spawn the CLI elsewhere', accepted 2026-07-29, in full house style: Context with a measurement table, three Options (resident daemon / link-and-spawn / C-ABI shared library) with honest Pro-Con bullets, Decision, Why, and a Revisit-when. JSON contract preserved: 'bytes' and 'bytes_to_capture' keep their exact prior values and meaning; apparent_bytes, allocated_bytes, cloned_bytes, copied_bytes, allocated_to_capture were added alongside. cargo test -p cs-archive 36 passed 0 failed (33 baseline + 3).

FINDING, independently verified: allocated blocks does NOT reduce the figure. Measured over the real 1057-file archive, allocated/apparent is 1.0010 (2268.2 MB vs 2270.4 MB) — these transcripts are neither sparse nor compressed, so blocks()*512 is len() rounded up to 4 KB. Also confirmed by direct experiment that an APFS clonefile destination reports the source's full st_blocks (both 1528 blocks / 782336 bytes for a 780000-byte file), so no stat-based figure can observe the block sharing at all. The clone/copy split from CaptureKind is therefore the only thing that expresses real marginal cost, and on this machine every capture clones, so the report now honestly reads '0.0 MB new on disk' where it used to read '0.7 MB captured'.

Corrected two counts in the spec I gave it, both verified against the archive: there are 15 chats/session-*.json files (not 13) and 15 checkpoints (not 17); logs.json at 4 and the 34 total were right. That duplication drove a design call worth keeping: message native_id is the record's own UUID rather than a per-file ordinal, so the index's INSERT OR IGNORE folds the second copy instead of doubling the conversation. model.rs sanctions this — it asks for file-scoped ids only where the source's own id is file-unique, and Gemini's is a UUID. An ordinal fallback covers a missing or repeated id, which would otherwise be swallowed silently by that same INSERT OR IGNORE.

Landed 2026-07-30. Highlighting now asks SQLite rather than re-implementing Porter — a scratch fts5 table declared with the identical tokenizer, so agreement with the ranker is structural rather than hoped for. The agent measured the alternative before rejecting it: over the 30,000 most frequent words of the real corpus, SQLite's porter and rust-stemmers' Porter2 disagree on 1,140 words (3.8%), and of ~21.7k word pairs one stemmer groups, 1,425 are grouped by only one of them — the same bug class being fixed.

Decisive test: every_row_the_ranker_returns_has_something_to_highlight builds an in-memory index and asserts, for commits/'Commit current changes', learning/'I learned about', running/'runs', cafe/'café' and general/'generated', that the ranker returns the row AND the highlighter marks something. Held for all 789 rows across six queries against the real corpus.

Also: spans honour a trailing prefix star, read back off to_match_expr_opts rather than re-derived, so a typeahead query does not label every in-progress word unmatched. An unlocatable match is now labelled rather than silently rendering the head of the message, which was the original defect.

Cost: snippet building is 5-20x the ranking, because each one inserts its message into the scratch table. Mitigated in the TUI by deferring snippets to expansion (nested=0 per keystroke); the structural fix is chat-search-6eb.30.

Landed 2026-07-30. Fenced blocks render dim behind a two-column rule (section 8 treatment, no dependency; syntect measured at +2.1MB and ~110us/line to colour the 3.9% of prose messages that tag a language). Match highlight takes Color::Blue from the indexed palette - index 4 is the slot Solarized fills with #268BD2, so a Solarized terminal gets that exact hue and every other terminal inherits its own; DIM is subtracted so a match never recedes inside dim snippet or code text. Preview body text now wraps at word boundaries instead of truncating, which forced the real fix: Preview::layout is the single source of geometry, returning each drawn row paired with the message that put it there, so what is drawn, what a click resolves to and what scrolling counts cannot drift. Scroll is clamped to the last screenful, its height memoised per width and invalidated on every fold, and the event loop absorbs an input burst into one frame and survives a transient unreadable event instead of ending the session. Verified against the real 2,980-conversation index and a 168,000-notch stress harness across 7 pane sizes. 363 tests passing (317 at the start of this work), zero warnings.

Implemented and verified end to end against the real archive on 2026-07-30: 106 archived files -> 14 conversations, 1,200 messages, 203 prose, 0 off-head-path. Titles and models land from the state file, timestamps from the audit clock, and cs search returns them under a claude.app badge.

Three findings worth carrying forward, all recorded in docs/FORMAT-NOTES.md:
- A transcript carries TWO session ids and the one matching the directory is the minority holder (19 records vs 405 for the CLI session underneath). Keying on either splits the conversation, so the importer keys on the local_<uuid> path segment.
- Repeated uuids are almost entirely isReplay turns re-emitted on resume, not corruption.
- The acceptance criterion 'widening the claude-code glob imports zero' was WRONG and the test now pins the truth: claude_code::import already accepts both sessionId and session_id, so it parses these files happily and files them under the wrong source with a claude --resume command that cannot reopen a desktop session, and without titles. The failure looks like success, which is the reason to keep two importers.

Landed 2026-07-30 as ce6bee8. spans_many marks a whole conversation in one transaction and one query instead of one call per message. Load on the corpus longest conversation (1,468 drawn blocks, 942 KB): 188 ms -> 94 ms, with the marking portion going ~144 ms -> ~50 ms. The stress harness of 168,000 scroll notches went 17.6 s -> 6.1 s.

The design note on this bead proposed lazy/viewport marking; batching got most of the win for far less risk, so lazy marking was not needed. Two hazards handled: the delimiter pool is shared across a batch and so is drawn from the whole of C0 rather than six characters, and an exhausted pool falls back to per-message marking rather than costing the whole conversation its marks. Verified against the real index - 21,124 messages across five queries produced byte-identical marks either way.

The remaining open cost is now SQL read and hydration (~44 ms), not marking. chat-search-6eb.30 (external-content fts5) would remove the insert entirely.

Closed 2026-07-30 without windowing the layout, which measurement said was the wrong fix.

The 51 ms was not the breadth of the work but a quadratic loop inside it: prefix_end re-measured the whole prefix for every character, ~w²/2 width lookups per row, ~42M over the 9,261 rows of the longest conversation. A printable-ASCII fast path takes layout to 22.6 ms. Selecting that conversation - load, marking and first frame - is now 82 ms against 240 ms before this and the batching in me9.1.1.6; a scroll frame is 2.9 ms p50; the stress harness of 168,000 notches is 4.2 s against 67 s at the start.

Windowing was prototyped far enough to price it. A height-only pass measured 65% of a full layout before the fix and ~43% after, so it would now save ~13 ms on the cold path only, and it would cost the single-source-of-geometry property: block_at_row and follow_focus reading a height derived separately from the rows drawn is exactly the arrangement that put clicks on the wrong message. Not worth it. The scaffolding (text::wrapped_rows) was removed rather than left as unused API.

Reopen if the cold path matters again - the note above records where the remaining time is (SQL read and hydration, ~44 ms).

Removed by chat-search-6eb.31.5, but the original framing was wrong and is worth correcting rather than closing quietly. The two derivations were real — search() blanked its query text before asking is_blank, rebuild_rows asked the raw query — but the effect was NOT observable. rows::build only adds hit rows for groups that have hits, and the browse path comes from recent(), which returns groups with hits: Vec::new(). So both row vectors came out identical either way. Latent inconsistency, not a user-visible bug. Fixed as one value read in both places, and pinned by one_query_decides_whether_the_list_is_matches_or_recent so it stays one.

Enter now execs the resume command with all three descriptors inherited (never redirected, which is what breaks crossterm). URLs go to the platform opener; cwd is set via current_dir rather than a composed 'cd &&'; Windows spawns and waits. Printing is kept for --print and whenever stdin/stdout is not a terminal, so eval "$(cs tui)" still works. Verified end-to-end under a pty against real codex.

If the git-root derivation is ever wanted it must be captured at import time from something in the archive, which is a different and larger bead than this one.
